#Define path variable to locate files on local machine:
```{r}
path <- "~/Desktop/GAD_ELN/DO/Data/Amplicon_Sequences/Project_LBAG_TODO_LP_MP1/Target_ITS/"
list.files(path)
```

#First pre-filter preparation:
    #generate matched lists of the forward and reverse read files
    #parse sample names from sequence file names
```{r}
fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern = "R1.fastq.gz", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern = "R2.fastq.gz", full.names = TRUE))
```

#Designate primer sequences:
```{r}
FWD <- "AGAACTTTYRRCAAYGGATCWCT"
REV <- "AGAGCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGCTTAART"
```

#Check the presence and orientation of these primers in amplicon sequences:
```{r}
allOrients <- function(primer) {
  # Create all orientations of the input sequence
  require(Biostrings)
  dna <- DNAString(primer)  # The Biostrings works w/ DNAString objects rather than character vectors
  orients <- c(Forward = dna, Complement = complement(dna), Reverse = reverse(dna), 
               RevComp = reverseComplement(dna))
  return(sapply(orients, toString))  # Convert back to character vector
}
FWD.orients <- allOrients(FWD)
REV.orients <- allOrients(REV)
FWD.orients
```

#First pre-filter: Remove sequences with ambiguous bases (N):
```{r}
fnFs.filtN <- file.path(path, "filtN", basename(fnFs)) # Put N-filterd files in filtN/ subdirectory
fnRs.filtN <- file.path(path, "filtN", basename(fnRs))
filterAndTrim(fnFs, fnFs.filtN, fnRs, fnRs.filtN, maxN = 0, multithread = TRUE, compress = TRUE)
```

#Count the number of times primers appear in forward and reverse reads of sequences,
#while considering all possible primer orientations.
#Identifying and counting primers on one set of paired end FASTQ files is sufficient,
#assuming all the files were created using the same library preparation.
#Thus, only process the first sample.
```{r}
primerHits <- function(primer, fn) {
  # Counts number of reads in which the primer is found
  nhits <- vcountPattern(primer, sread(readFastq(fn)), fixed = FALSE)
  return(sum(nhits > 0))
}
rbind(FWD.ForwardReads = sapply(FWD.orients, primerHits, fn = fnFs.filtN[[1]]), 
      FWD.ReverseReads = sapply(FWD.orients, primerHits, fn = fnRs.filtN[[1]]), 
      REV.ForwardReads = sapply(REV.orients, primerHits, fn = fnFs.filtN[[1]]), 
      REV.ReverseReads = sapply(REV.orients, primerHits, fn = fnRs.filtN[[1]]))
```

#Some reverse reads? amplicons are large, up to 600bp.

#Define and test path to cutadapt
```{r}
cutadapt <- "/Users/gadlott/.local/bin/cutadapt"
system2(cutadapt, args = "--version")
```

#Create output filenames for the cutadapt-ed files,
#and define the parameters we are going to give the cutadapt command.
#The critical parameters are the primers,
#and they need to be in the right orientation,
#i.e. the FWD primer should have been matching the forward-reads in its forward orientation,
#and the REV primer should have been matching the reverse-reads in its forward orientation.
```{r}
path.cut <- file.path(path, "cutadapt")
if(!dir.exists(path.cut)) dir.create(path.cut)
fnFs.cut <- file.path(path.cut, basename(fnFs))
fnRs.cut <- file.path(path.cut, basename(fnRs))

FWD.RC <- dada2:::rc(FWD)
REV.RC <- dada2:::rc(REV)
# Trim FWD and the reverse-complement of REV off of R1 (forward reads)
R1.flags <- paste("-g", FWD, "-a", REV.RC) 
# Trim REV and the reverse-complement of FWD off of R2 (reverse reads)
R2.flags <- paste("-G", REV, "-A", FWD.RC) 
# Run Cutadapt
for(i in seq_along(fnFs)) {
  system2(cutadapt, args = c(R1.flags, R2.flags, "-n", 2, "-m", 100,
                             "-o", fnFs.cut[i], "-p", fnRs.cut[i], # output files
                             fnFs.filtN[i], fnRs.filtN[i])) # input files
}
```

#As a sanity check, count the presence of primers in the first cutadapt-ed sample:
```{r}
rbind(FWD.ForwardReads = sapply(FWD.orients, primerHits, fn = fnFs.cut[[1]]), 
      FWD.ReverseReads = sapply(FWD.orients, primerHits, fn = fnRs.cut[[1]]), 
      REV.ForwardReads = sapply(REV.orients, primerHits, fn = fnFs.cut[[1]]), 
      REV.ReverseReads = sapply(REV.orients, primerHits, fn = fnRs.cut[[1]]))
```

#The primer-free sequence files are now ready to be analyzed through the DADA2 pipeline.

#proceedingto DADA2.

#read in the names of the cutadapt-ed FASTQ files and apply string manipulation
#to get matched lists of forward and reverse fastq files:
```{r}
# Forward and reverse fastq filenames have the format:
cutFs <- sort(list.files(path.cut, pattern = "_R1.fastq.gz", full.names = TRUE))
cutRs <- sort(list.files(path.cut, pattern = "_R2.fastq.gz", full.names = TRUE))
```

#Inspect read quality profiles

```{r}
plotQualityProfile(cutFs[2])
```

#strange pattern - two distinct bands?

#Visualize the quality profiles of the reverse reads:
```{r}
plotQualityProfile(cutRs[2])
```

#Assign the filenames for the output of the filtered reads to be stored as fastq.gz files:
```{r}
filtFs <- file.path(path.cut, "filtered", basename(cutFs))
filtRs <- file.path(path.cut, "filtered", basename(cutRs))
```

#Filter and trim the files, using the following settings:
    #maxN=0 (DADA2 requires sequences contain no Ns),
    #truncQ = 2,
    #rm.phix = TRUE,
    #maxEE=2.
    #truncation on forward reads at bp=240, reverse reads at bp=160  ()
#Note: We enforce a minLen here, to get rid of spurious very low-length sequences.
```{r}
out <- filterAndTrim(cutFs, filtFs, cutRs, filtRs, maxN = 0, truncQ = 2, minLen = 100, rm.phix = TRUE, compress = TRUE, multithread = TRUE)
head(out)

```

#Learn the forward-read error rates:
```{r}
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, multithread = TRUE)
```

#Learn the reverse-read error rates:
```{r}
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread = TRUE)
```

#Visualize the estimated error rates as a sanity check.
```{r}
plotErrors(errF, nominalQ = TRUE)
```
#seems pretty bad to me - still have no concept of how to evaluate this. Will need to see how it looks on full data.

#Dereplicate identical reads:
```{r}
derepFs <- derepFastq(filtFs, verbose = TRUE)
derepRs <- derepFastq(filtRs, verbose = TRUE)
# Name the derep-class objects by the sample names
names(derepFs) <- sample.names
names(derepRs) <- sample.names
```

#Sample Inference

#At this step, the core sample inference algorithm is applied to the dereplicated data:
```{r}
dadaFs <- dada(derepFs, err = errF, multithread = TRUE)
dadaRs <- dada(derepRs, err = errR, multithread = TRUE)
```

#merge paired reads
```{r}
mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, derepFs, dadaRs, derepRs, verbose=TRUE)
```

#Construct sequence table
    #We can now construct an amplicon sequence variant table (ASV) table,
    #a higher-resolution version of the OTU table produced by traditional methods.
```{r}
seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
dim(seqtab)
```

#Remove chimeras
```{r}
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method="consensus", multithread=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
```

#save ASV table:
```{r}
write_rds(seqtab.nochim, "Results/ASV_Table_ITS.rds")
```


#Inspect distribution of sequence lengths:
```{r}
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab.nochim)))
```

#shockingly variable, and some seem pretty small?

#Track reads through the entire pipeline:
```{r}
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))
track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN), sapply(mergers, 
                                                                       getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim))
# If processing a single sample, remove the sapply calls: e.g. replace
# sapply(dadaFs, getN) with getN(dadaFs)
colnames(track) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", 
                     "nonchim")
rownames(track) <- sample.names
track

track2 <- as.data.frame(track)
track2$Sequencing_ID <- row.names(track)

write_csv(track2, "Results/DADA2_pipeline_track_ITS.csv")
```


```{r}
system.time(
  taxa <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim, unite.ref, multithread = TRUE, tryRC = TRUE)
```
